questions.q: What does const double3 = (n) => n * 2; return when called?
options: The function itself, not its result
n * 2 — the expression's value is implicitly returned since there are no braces
A syntax error, since arrow functions require braces
undefined, because there's no explicit return keyword
questions.explain: A single-expression arrow function body with no braces implicitly returns the expression's value.

questions.q: What is the real, practical reason arrow functions are preferred for callbacks inside class methods?
options: They don't have their own `this` — they inherit it from the surrounding scope, unlike regular functions whose `this` depends on how they're called
They run measurably faster than regular functions
Arrow functions are required by the JavaScript spec inside classes
Regular functions cannot accept any parameters
questions.explain: Lexical `this` is the substantive difference — not just that arrow functions are shorter to type.

questions.q: Given const [first, , third] = [10, 20, 30];, what are the values of first and third?
options: first is 20, third is 30
first is 10, third is 30 — the empty slot skips the middle element
first is 10, third is 20
This throws a syntax error
questions.explain: An empty slot in array destructuring skips that position without assigning it to a variable.

questions.q: What does const { value: amount } = transaction; do?
options: Deletes the value property from the original transaction object
Creates two separate variables, value and amount, both holding the same data
Throws an error because renaming during destructuring isn't allowed
Destructures the value property off transaction but stores it in a new variable named amount
questions.explain: The `property: newName` syntax renames a destructured variable without changing the original object.

questions.q: In const { gasPrice = 0n } = transaction;, when does gasPrice get the value 0n?
options: Only when transaction.gasPrice is missing or undefined
Only if transaction itself is undefined
Never — defaults aren't supported in object destructuring
Every single time, regardless of what transaction.gasPrice actually holds
questions.explain: A destructuring default applies specifically when the property is missing or explicitly undefined.
